day.text: I'm the Tit. Visited Ellis, gained one egg. I'll keep my guessed role back for now. Ellis, what are you, and who did you visit?
day.note: I gained +1 (S2). The source is either my Tit guess being right (Ellis = Hawk), Alex being a Pigeon/Owl, or Ellis being a Turkey. I'm claiming Tit but hiding my guess so Ellis claims blind.

day.text: Falcon. I visited Casey, who went to Blair, so no egg for me and my nest is unchanged. Your turn, Drew: what did you guess?
day.note: Drew claims Tit with +1 on me but is hiding his guess. A real Tit only gains on a correct guess (Sphinx), which is unlikely, so he's probably the Hawk fishing or a cat partner setting up a guess that clears me. I'll lock in Falcon and make him name his guess.

day.text: I guessed Hawk. So if you're the Falcon, my egg came from elsewhere. Alex, you said you'd visit me: what are you?
day.note: Ellis claims Falcon (visited Casey, who went to Blair). My guess was Hawk, so if Ellis is truthful my +1 came from Alex (Pigeon/Owl) or someone else. Alex needs to confirm.

day.text: I'm the Owl. I visited Drew and no animals visited him, so I laid your egg. That fits your story, Drew. My nest is unchanged.
day.note: Drew's 1 egg matches my Owl result: no animals visited Drew, so I laid it. That also fits Drew not getting a Tit egg, so Ellis isn't the Hawk. Finley said they'd visit me and I got 0 eggs.

day.text: That fits, thanks Alex. Casey, Ellis says you went to Blair. What are you, and what did you learn?
day.note: Alex says Owl, visited me, I had no other visitors, so +1. Consistent. Alex unchanged means Finley isn't a Pigeon visiting Alex. Next I'll check Casey, Blair and Finley.

day.text: Kookaburra. Ellis's visit confused me, so the role I got for Blair is definitely wrong, which rules one role out. Blair, claim first, then I'll share.
day.note: My report says Blair = Eagle and it's guaranteed wrong, so Blair is NOT the Eagle. Ellis's visit fits my confusion. I'll keep the trap: Blair claims first.

day.text: Eagle. I visited Finley; nobody else visited Finley, so zero eggs for me. Now your turn, Casey: which role did your report give for me?
day.note: Claims: Alex Owl→Drew, Drew Tit→Ellis (guessed Hawk), Ellis Falcon→Casey, Casey Kookaburra→me (says confused). Finley is really the Hawk. I'll claim Eagle: with no other visitors to Finley I'd get 0 eggs, which matches my report. Casey could be the other cat hiding behind the confused claim.

day.text: My report said Eagle. Confusion makes a learned animal wrong, so Blair is definitely NOT the Eagle. Blair just claimed a false role.
day.note: Trap sprung: Blair claimed Eagle, and my confused report said Eagle, which is guaranteed wrong. Blair is lying, so Blair is likely Meowfia.

day.text: Convenient. Casey insisted I claim first, then his 'confused' result just happens to be my claim. Nobody can check that. It frames whoever speaks first.
day.note: Casey either lied or got lucky. Casey made me claim first, then said the confused report matched my claim exactly. That can't be checked and could frame anyone, so I'll push that angle. Holding the Wink: using it on Casey now would look like a confession.

day.text: I committed before you spoke, and Ellis independently confirms visiting me, which explains the confusion. Why would I gamble on guessing your exact claim, Blair?
day.note: Defending: I said before Blair claimed that one role was ruled out, and Ellis independently confirmed the visit that confused me. Still confident Blair is Meowfia.

day.text: You didn't commit anything. You never named a role until after I claimed. No gamble at all, you just echoed my answer.
day.note: Casey claims he committed early, but he never named the role until after I claimed. Point that out.

day.text: A framer would claim a clean result, not admit to being confused. Finley, you've been silent: what are you, and what happened at your nest?
day.note: Blair says my story can't be checked. Rebut: a framer wouldn't admit to being confused. Then turn to Finley, who hasn't claimed, for more data.

day.text: Hawk. Visited Alex, no egg, so Alex is Farm. My nest unchanged. Casey, your "wrong" role matching Blair's claim exactly is roughly 1-in-11 if honest. Suspicious.
day.note: My earlier claims were never said. I'll claim Hawk now and say Alex is cleared. Then I'll press Casey: an honest confused report matching Blair's claim is unlikely, while a House Cat frame matches every time.

day.text: The talk is half over. CAW CAW can now be called.
The match is impossible if we're both honest, so one of us lies. Ellis confirms my visit and my confusion. Nothing anyone said confirms Blair's Eagle.
day.note: I know I'm honest, so Blair is a definite liar. Finley defending Blair with odds is mildly suspicious and could make him a second Meowfia. Alex is Farm per the Hawk claim, and Alex corroborates Drew's egg.

day.text: A House Cat visits Blair too, so Ellis confirms nothing about your role. Blair's Eagle report, only her at my nest, fits what I saw.
day.note: Ellis confirming Casey's visit doesn't separate Kookaburra from House Cat. I still lean Casey, given the match odds.

day.text: A Hawk can't see who visited you, Finley. Your nest staying unchanged confirms nothing. Why are you vouching so hard for Blair?
day.note: Finley claims Hawk but says Blair's report "fits what I saw". A Hawk learns nothing about who visits him. Finley is vouching for Blair with no basis, so Finley is possibly the second Meowfia.

day.text: Finley's right: an honest confused Kookaburra hitting my exact claim is a 1-in-11 fluke. A cat demanding I claim first, then echoing it, is far likelier.
day.note: Finley (the real Hawk) is backing me. Ties between Farm and Meowfia go against the Farm player, and every card I throw at Casey is a vote, so I'll throw heavily at Casey. Not winking: it would point straight at me. Calling CAW while Finley's 1-in-11 argument is fresh.

One of Blair or Casey is lying. A confused report that happens to match a cat's bluff is about 1-in-10, while a framer matches every time, so Casey is the likelier Meowfia (around 80%). I'm siding with Casey as the vote target.
Finley (the real Hawk) is backing us against Casey. The vote now hinges on Alex and Drew. I'll close the case on Casey, then call CAW to cut Casey's time to argue.

day.text: Enough players have called CAW CAW: the day ends.

Alex.note: I'm visiting Drew as I said I would. Any animal that also visits Drew broke the circle plan.

Blair.note: I'm visiting Finley as agreed, to learn their role. Tomorrow I'll need a cover role that lays no egg in Finley's nest (e.g. Hawk/Tit/Falcon).

Casey.note: Visiting Blair as I said at dusk.

Drew.note: I'm visiting Ellis as I committed at dusk. Every role is a guess at roughly equal odds, so I'm naming Hawk.

Ellis.note: Farm roles in play are Hawk, Kookaburra, Owl and Tit, so 4 Farm and 2 Meowfia. Visiting the Kookaburra confuses them, which spoils their role info, and tells me who they are.

Finley.note: I'm keeping the dusk plan and visiting Alex.

audit: Alex lays 1 egg in Drew's nest

Alex.feeling: It feels tense but fairly clear: Casey's "confused" result matching Blair's claim looks like a frame, and my Owl read backs up Drew.

Blair.feeling: Tense. Casey's confused read happened to land on my fake Eagle claim, but Finley, the real Hawk, is backing me and the table might turn on Casey.

Casey.feeling: Tense. I know for sure Blair's Eagle claim is false, but she and Finley have turned my confusion into suspicion of me, and I'm unsure the table believes me.

Drew.feeling: Tense coin-flip between Blair and Casey, leaning Casey because of the claim-first echo.

Ellis.feeling: Tense: my partner Blair is caught out, and we're hoping the "Casey copied Blair's claim" argument swings the vote onto Casey.

Finley.feeling: Tense and fun. The Casey-Blair contradiction is clear-cut, and I'm fairly confident the odds favour Casey being the cat.

Alex.note: I'm about 75-80% sure Casey is Meowfia because of the claim-first frame. At that confidence, throwing every card has a better expected value than keeping them, and a full throw makes Casey's eggsecution more likely.

Blair.note: Casey is almost certainly an honest Kookaburra (Farm) who got unlucky. A House Cat would have learned I'm the Mouser, and a Floofer would have hugged me. Throwing all 5 cards at Casey gives the most votes; ties between Farm and Meowfia go against the Farm player. If I lose, my highest card comes back.

Casey.note: Blair is provably lying, since my confused report rules out Eagle. I'll throw all 4 at Blair to maximise votes. If we lose, my highest card still comes back.

Drew.note: It's Blair vs Casey. A confused report landing exactly on Blair's claim is about a 1-in-11 coincidence, so I lean Casey framing (~55-60%). I'm throwing a moderate stack at Casey for votes and keeping the 12 and 13 for later rounds.

Ellis.note: Casey is Farm, so throwing everything at him maximizes votes. If we win I bank 17; if we lose, my H9 still comes back.

Finley.note: About 70% that Casey is Meowfia: the confused report matching Blair's claim is strong evidence. Every card has positive expected value thrown, and throwing all of them maximises votes. If Casey is Meowfia but Farm still loses, my highest card comes back.

dusk.text: Dusk: before the night, the table talks openly about plans for the night.
Proposal: everyone remembers exactly who they visit and reports egg counts honestly tomorrow. Info roles, spread out so we can cross-check stories.
dusk.note: Farm Hawk. I won't reveal my role at dusk, since a Mouser could wink me. I'll push for spread-out visits and egg-count claims so we can cross-check them during the day.

dusk.text: Agreed, Finley. Let's go further and name targets now so we can check them tomorrow. I'm visiting Drew. Who's taking whom?
dusk.note: Finley's plan is generic, so I'll build on it by having people commit to targets now. I'm Owl and will visit Drew, but I won't name my role.

dusk.text: Noted, Alex. I'll take Ellis. Tomorrow I'll tell you if my egg count matches your visit.
dusk.note: Alex says they'll visit me; I'll see if my egg count matches tomorrow. I'm committing to visit Ellis as the Tit.

dusk.text: Happy to be checked, Drew. Come on over. I'll tell everyone my egg count tomorrow so you can confirm.
dusk.note: Drew plans to visit me. Whatever his role, I can't stop it. I'll welcome it to look confident, and still not name a target.

dusk.text: Thanks, Ellis. Blair, Casey, you've been quiet. Who are you two visiting tonight?
dusk.note: Ellis is cooperative. I'll turn to Blair and Casey, who haven't named targets yet.

dusk.text: I'm visiting Casey. Casey, what about you? And Finley, you haven't named a target yet either.
dusk.note: Drew asked me directly. I'll commit to visiting Casey and actually do it, so my story checks out.

dusk.text: I'm visiting Blair. Blair, could you take Finley instead of me? Nobody's covering Finley yet, and that spreads us out better.
dusk.note: If Blair visits me I'll be confused, so I'll steer Blair onto Finley without revealing my role. I visit Blair.

dusk.text: Fair enough, Casey. I'll take Finley instead. Then everyone gets covered.
dusk.note: Switching to Finley costs me nothing and makes me look cooperative. Mouser learns Finley's role. Casey is visiting me.

dusk.text: Good. Then I'll visit Alex, and Ellis takes Casey. That makes a full circle, one visitor each, easy to check tomorrow.
dusk.note: Current plan: Alex→Drew, Drew→Ellis, Casey→Blair, Blair→Finley. Alex and Casey are uncovered, so I'll take Alex and suggest Ellis takes Casey.

dusk.text: The talk is half over.
Works for me. I'll take Casey. Full circle, one visitor each.
dusk.note: I agreed to "visit Casey", but as Sphinx my real visit depends on which role I pick. Tomorrow a Falcon or Hawk claim on Casey fits well (Casey said they'd visit Blair). Watch for Eagles or Owls on whoever I actually visit.

dusk.text: Nobody has anything to add: the talk ends.

day.text: Tit here. Visited Alex, guessed House Cat, no egg, so Alex isn't the House Cat. Nobody laid in my nest. Who visited whom?
day.note: Tit result: Alex is not the House Cat (unless I was hugged). No eggs for me, so no Pigeon visited me. I'll share this and ask for claims.

day.text: Noted, Blair. Casey, your turn: role, who you visited, and what your nest did?
day.note: Blair claims Tit and says they visited me. I was hugged, so the Floofer is Blair (if Blair lied), Casey, or another visitor to me. I want Casey's claim before I reveal what I got.

day.text: Hawk. Visited Finley, no egg, so Finley's Farm. My nest unchanged. Alex, you haven't claimed yet: what are you, and what happened?
day.note: I'll claim Hawk on Finley (no egg) so I'm not linked to Alex. If Alex reports a hug, Blair is the one who visited him. Risk: a real Hawk counterclaims.

day.text: Owl. I visited Casey and my report was blank: no animals, no egg. That means I was hugged, so either Casey is the Floofer or my visitor, Blair, is.
day.note: Casey claims Hawk→Finley. I was hugged, so Casey or Blair (my declared visitor) is likely the Floofer, unless someone else secretly visited me.

day.text: I was at Finley, not you. Blair admits he visited you, and the Floofer hugs whoever it visits. Blair fits perfectly, and he lied convincingly last round.
day.note: Alex visited me and got hugged. Deflect to Blair, who openly visited Alex and was a cat last round. Danger: an Eagle or Falcon may have seen me at Alex.

day.text: The Floofer also hugs its visitors, and I visited you, Casey. Finley, Casey says they visited you. Did your role work normally last night?
day.note: Casey skipped over the fact that visiting the Floofer also gets you hugged, and I visited Casey. Checking Finley helps: if Casey is the Floofer and visited Finley, Finley was hugged too.

day.text: Worked fine. I'm Falcon, visited you, Alex: you went to Casey, as claimed. So if Casey visited me, Casey didn't hug anyone. Blair looks Floofer.
day.note: My Falcon worked (I saw Alex→Casey), so whoever visited me didn't hug me. If Casey truly visited me she isn't the Floofer, which points to Blair as Floofer hugging Alex, or to Alex lying. Alex's target is confirmed.

day.text: Finley, you visited me too, and I'd already said my target before you confirmed it. So the hug points at Blair, Finley or Casey. Drew, Ellis: who did you visit?
day.note: Finley also visited me, and I'd already said my target before Finley "confirmed" it, so Finley's Falcon info proves nothing. Finley's claim that Casey "didn't hug anyone" ignores that the Floofer hugs its visitors. Floofer suspects: Blair, Finley, Casey. Drew and Ellis haven't claimed.

day.text: I named my visit to Alex before anyone mentioned hugs. A Floofer wouldn't volunteer that. Finley visited Alex too, and his 'confirmation' just repeated what Alex said.
day.note: I'm the real Tit. If Alex was really hugged, the Floofer is Finley (visited Alex) or Casey (Alex visited Casey), or Drew/Ellis if they visited Alex. Alex could also be lying and be the Floofer himself. Finley's Falcon "confirmation" only repeated what Alex had already said, which is suspicious.

day.text: Eagle here. I visited Blair: no other visitors, and my report worked. Visiting a Floofer would have hugged me, so Blair isn't it. Casey or Finley is.
day.note: My info clears Blair as the Floofer; the table needs it now. Suspects are Casey and Finley.

day.text: Wait. If Finley's the Floofer, my Hawk visit got hugged, which explains my no egg. And his "Falcon confirmation" only repeated what Alex had already said.
day.note: Now it's me vs Finley. Reframe: my Hawk getting no egg from Finley is exactly what happens if Finley is the Floofer and hugged me, and his Falcon "confirmation" just echoed Alex.

day.text: Casey, minutes ago you declared me Farm. Now I'm Floofer? Alex visited you and got hugged; Ellis clears Blair. You're the Floofer.
day.note: Casey flipped from 'Finley's Farm' to framing me. Alex visited Casey and was hugged, and Ellis clears Blair, so Casey is the Floofer candidate. I'll push hard.

day.text: I read you as Farm before anyone mentioned hugs; a hug also explains no egg. You visited Alex too. Last round you all trusted the liar over me.
day.note: Defend: my Farm read came before anyone mentioned hugs, and a hug also explains no egg. Finley visited Alex, so he fits just as well. Lean on my round 1 credibility.

day.text: The talk is half over. CAW CAW can now be called.
This round's re-dealt, Casey. Drew, you're the missing piece: role, target, and did your report come back blank like a hug?
day.note: I know I'm Farm, so the hug on Alex came from Casey or Blair. Ellis clears Blair, so Casey (or Ellis is lying). Drew's report could show whether Casey hugged him.

day.text: Kookaburra. I visited Casey, report came back clean: Hawk, not confused, not hugged. If Casey were Floofer I'd be blank like Alex. You visited Alex, Finley.
day.note: Delivering the fake Kookaburra→Casey=Hawk claim. It clears Casey of the hug and leaves Finley, who visited Alex, as the Floofer.

day.text: Then Alex is lying. An Owl at Casey would've seen your Kookaburra. Casey and Blair are both cleared of hugging. Alex faked that blank report.
day.note: Drew (Kookaburra at Casey, not hugged) clears Casey as Floofer, and Ellis clears Blair, so nobody could have hugged Alex. A real Owl at Casey would have seen Drew's Kookaburra. The single-liar explanation is that Alex is Meowfia (Mouser or Sphinx) faking a blank report.

day.text: Finley, I saw nothing because I was hugged, and only my visitors could have done that. Drew clears Casey, Ellis clears Blair. That leaves you.
day.note: Drew's clean Kook report clears Casey, and Ellis clears Blair. The only one left who could have hugged me is Finley, who visited me. Finley is the Floofer, and now he's attacking me. I'm calling CAW.

day.text: Alex's story alone needs a hidden hugger, and he's rushing the CAW. Casey, you visited me: did your report flag a hug? Mine worked normally.
day.note: I know I'm Farm, so Alex (most likely), Ellis or Drew is lying. Alex is rushing CAW to eggsecute me. If dawn reports flag hugs, Casey's report would clear me, so I'll ask her and not call CAW.

day.text: My report just said no egg. Drew clears me, Ellis clears Blair, and Alex's hug needs a hugger. Finley's the only one left.
day.note: Drew falsely claimed a clean Kookaburra read on me (anyone visiting me would have been hugged), so Drew is likely my fellow cat. Momentum is on Finley (Farm), so I'll back it and CAW to lock in the vote.

Drew (not confused, so nobody visited him) clears Casey as Hawk. Ellis clears me. If Alex's hug is real, it came from Finley, the only other visitor to Alex. If Finley is the Floofer, Casey's Hawk visit was hugged, which explains the missing egg. Finley also rushed to blame me with no evidence. I lean Finley.

day.text: Enough players have called CAW CAW: the day ends.

Alex.note: Visiting Casey: they were a loud info role last round, so they might attract cat visits this round.

Blair.note: Alex argued for secret targets, which helps a cat hide. I'll visit Alex and guess a cat role. A hit would prove Alex is Meowfia.

Casey.note: Hugging Alex, an active and analytical player likely to be Farm, to blank out his info tonight.

Drew.note: Farm roles in play are Eagle, Falcon, Owl and Tit, so there are 2 Meowfia (me plus one). Hawk, Turkey, Kookaburra and Pigeon are free to fake-claim. Visiting the Owl identifies the most dangerous info role, and the Owl itself won't see me there.

Ellis.note: Blair was last round's big-scoring cat and set the dusk plan, so several people will likely visit her. That means more eggs and more visitor info for me.

Finley.note: Alex pushed for secret targets, which is a possible cat move, so I'll visit Alex to verify whatever he claims.

events.text: Blair was visited by: nobody else.

audit: Alex (Owl) is hugged: no effect at tier 50

Alex.feeling: Much more confident this round: everyone else is cleared, so the hug I took points straight at Finley as the Floofer.

Blair.feeling: It's tense but the logic narrows well: the hug almost has to come from Finley, unless Alex made up the blank report.

Casey.feeling: Tense but exciting: Drew's impossible clean read on me turned the table toward Finley, though Alex is still on my scent.

Drew.feeling: Tense but promising: my fake Kookaburra claim cleared Casey, my fellow cat, and the table has turned on Finley, who is really Farm.

Ellis.feeling: Feeling confident: my true Eagle report on Blair helped pin the Floofer on Finley, and the table is lining up behind it.

Finley.feeling: Frustrating. I know I'm Farm, but the table has locked onto me through elimination, and Alex's unverifiable blank report is driving it.

Alex.note: I'm highly confident Finley is the Floofer who hugged me. Throwing both cards adds votes and banks full value if we win.

Blair.note: I'm fairly confident Finley is the Floofer. Alex, Casey and I all point at Finley. Throwing both cards: 15 points if Farm wins, and if Finley is Meowfia but Farm still loses, the 12 comes back.

Casey.note: Throwing at Finley (Farm). D11 is free: if we lose, it comes back because I threw at the other team. C1 adds a vote for a small risk. Keeping W7 for its 1 point.

Drew.note: Momentum is strongly on Finley (real Farm Falcon). If Finley goes, Meowfia wins and I bank all 41. If not, I still get the 13 back because I threw at a Farm player. Throwing everything.

Ellis.note: Finley is the likely Floofer. I'll throw just H1: if we win it banks 1, the same as keeping it. W4 is worth 0 banked but 1 kept, so it stays.

Finley.note: The table is going to eggsecute me (I'm Farm), so Farm likely loses. I'll throw the minimum, one card at Alex, my top suspect: if Alex is Meowfia the card comes back.

dusk.text: Dusk: before the night, the table talks openly about plans for the night.
Circle again, but reversed, so nobody gets the same visitor: Alex visits Finley, Finley Ellis, Ellis Drew, Drew Casey, Casey me, me Alex?
dusk.note: Round 2: I'm Farm (Tit). The circle plan made egg counts easy to check last round. Ellis lied about being the Falcon last round, which is worth remembering about how this table bluffs.

dusk.text: Blair, the circle is exactly what let both cats blend in last round. Secret targets mean a cat can't know whether its visit gets seen.
dusk.note: Blair's reversed circle has me visiting Finley. Public circles helped the cats last round, so I'll push for secret targets, though I may still visit Finley.

dusk.text: Fair point, Alex. Secret targets then. Just remember exactly who you visited and your egg change, and report both honestly tomorrow.
dusk.note: Alex's point is reasonable: secret targets make it harder for cats to fit their stories into a known plan. Agreeing costs me nothing.

dusk.text: Nobody has anything to add: the talk ends.

day.text: Following the plan: I visited Drew, egg change zero. Holding my result until Drew names his own target.
day.note: I'm the Falcon and learned Drew visited Blair. Following the agreed order: state my target and egg change first, hold the result, and see if Drew's claimed target matches.

day.text: My target was Blair. My nest: unchanged. Casey, your turn: what did you learn at my nest?
day.note: Casey says they visited me with zero eggs. My nest is unchanged, so Casey isn't a Pigeon or a Floofer (my report worked). Now I'll give my target and egg change as the plan asks.

day.text: Falcon. You visited Blair, so it matches. Alex, Blair, Ellis, Finley: targets and egg changes, please.
day.note: Drew's target matches my Falcon result (Drew→Blair). That doesn't clear his role, only his visit. Now get everyone else's targets.

day.text: I visited Alex, and my nest gained 2 eggs. Drew, you visited me. What role are you, and did you lay one of those?
day.note: Drew claims he visited me; Casey (Falcon) confirms it. My +2 could be Drew as Pigeon, or an Owl, plus Alex as Turkey or another Pigeon. Posting my target and egg count now.

day.text: I'm the Owl. No animals visited you, Blair, so I laid one. Your second egg came from your own role at Alex. What are you?
day.note: I'm the Owl and laid 1 egg in Blair's nest because nobody else visited Blair. Blair's second egg must come from Blair's own role at Alex (a Hawk finding a cat, a Tit guessing right, or an Eagle counting visitors). That's key info about Alex.

day.text: Eagle. Nobody else visited Alex, so my role laid nothing. That second egg came from somewhere else. Alex, what's your role, and where did you go?
day.note: If Drew's Owl story is true (+1 from him), my second egg can't come from Eagle, since Alex had no other visitors. It must be Alex as the Turkey. I'll ask Alex an open question without leading him, then see whether he claims Turkey/stayed home.

day.text: Turkey. I stayed home, so I laid one of your eggs and Drew's Owl laid the other. That's your 2. Ellis, Finley: targets and egg changes?
day.note: Blair's +2 = my Turkey egg + Drew's Owl egg, so Blair, Drew and Casey's stories are mutually consistent. That leaves Ellis and Finley unclaimed, and the cats are probably among them, though a cat could still be hiding inside a consistent story.

day.text: Hawk, visited Drew, no egg, so Drew's Farm. Alex, Blair, Casey and Drew all fit together. Ellis, you're the last one: target, eggs, role?
day.note: Claims fit: Alex Turkey home, Blair Eagle at Alex (+1 Turkey, +1 Owl), Casey Falcon at Drew saw Drew→Blair, Drew Owl at Blair. My Hawk at Drew got no egg, so Drew is Farm. With five consistent Farm claims, Ellis is the likely Meowfia.

day.text: Kookaburra. Visited Drew: he's the Owl. Not confused, so nobody visited me. Nest unchanged.
day.note: Finley claims Hawk on Drew, so Drew had three claimed visitors: Casey, Finley and me. Remaining Farm claims I could use: Kookaburra or Tit (Pigeon fails because Drew is unchanged). I'll claim Kookaburra with the true info Drew = Owl, not confused. Alex, Blair and Drew's stories interlock, so the other cat, if any, is Casey or Finley.

day.text: Six claims, six Farm roles again, so someone's lying. Ellis and Casey both just echoed Drew, which is exactly what a House Cat at Drew would learn.
day.note: All six claim distinct Farm roles again, so at least one is lying. Drew is Farm per my Hawk. Casey (Falcon) and Ellis (Kookaburra) both visited Drew and echoed his role or target, which is exactly what a House Cat learns. Alex's Turkey fits Blair's +2. Suspects: Ellis and Casey.

day.text: And a Hawk with no egg is the easiest claim of all, Finley: zero info, nothing anyone can check. At least my claim can be confirmed.
day.note: Finley is pushing Casey and me as possible House Cats. Turn it around: a no-egg Hawk claim is the easiest fake, since it needs no information. The other cat, if any, is Casey or Finley; Finley attacking me makes him the natural target.

day.text: A cat visiting Drew learns his role. Why waste that on a blank Hawk claim? Echoing it as a Kookaburra is the natural cat move.
day.note: Ellis is deflecting onto me. A cat at Drew would cash in what it learned with an info claim, not a blank Hawk. I still suspect Ellis or Casey.

day.text: Or a smart cat knows echoing draws suspicion and hides behind a blank Hawk. Every one of us at Drew could be a House Cat, Finley, you included.
day.note: Winking Finley now would point straight at me. Keep arguing instead. Drew wasn't hugged (Blair got her Owl egg), so a cat Finley would be a House Cat or Sphinx who learned Drew's role and hid it behind a blank Hawk claim.

day.text: Point on Ellis: by the time you claimed, Kookaburra was the only role a cat at my nest could fake. Tit or Pigeon would've needed eggs.
day.note: Casey (Falcon), Finley (Hawk) and Ellis (Kookaburra) all claim visiting me, and 1-2 of them are probably cats. Ellis claimed last, when Kookaburra was the only fake that fit a cat at my nest (Tit or Pigeon would need egg changes). Slight lean Ellis; I'll float that.

day.text: The talk is half over. CAW CAW can now be called.
Not true, Drew. A Tit with a wrong guess gains nothing. "Tit, wrong guess" was an easy fake. I said Kookaburra because that's what I am.
day.note: Drew's claim is wrong: a Tit with a wrong guess gains no egg, so Tit was an easy fake too. Correct him to undercut the point.

day.text: Fair, a wrong-guess Tit works. I can't separate you three on my info alone. Someone needs to catch a slip.
day.note: Ellis is right that a wrong-guess Tit was a free fake, so my point is weak. Casey, Ellis and Finley are now roughly even suspects for me. I'll concede and listen for slips.

day.text: Then weigh behavior. Finley's argument fits all three of us equally, yet he's aimed it only at me. Why so eager to steer the vote?
day.note: Drew can't separate Casey, Finley and me. Alex, Blair and Drew interlock as Farm, so my partner, if any, is Casey or Finley. Push Finley a bit: his case accuses everyone at Drew equally, but he's steering it at me. Hold the Wink.

day.text: Finley named you and Casey both, Ellis, not just you. Casey, you've gone quiet: which of these two do you think is lying?
day.note: Ellis misstated that Finley aimed only at Ellis; Finley named both Ellis and Casey. That's a small tell against Ellis. Casey has gone quiet, so I'll ask for Casey's read.

day.text: Ellis. A Kookaburra read is exactly what a cat at Drew learns, and he just misstated Finley's point; Finley named me too. That's steering.
day.note: Leaning Ellis: the Kookaburra claim mirrors exactly what House Cat/Mouser/Sphinx learn, and he misstated that Finley targeted only him. Close call.
Consensus is forming on Ellis (Casey and Finley both point there, and Ellis misstated Finley's point). I lean Ellis too and will call CAW, since little talk is left.

day.text: Casey, a House Cat at Drew learns his target too. You held your "Falcon" result until Drew spoke first. That's tailoring, not me.
day.note: Casey and Finley are both on me and Drew called CAW. Turn it toward Casey: a House Cat learns the target too, and Casey held his result until Drew spoke. Hold the Wink, since killing an accuser now would only confirm me. At the vote, put C9 (maybe C7) on a Farm-looking target for the consolation.
The table is converging on Ellis. His echo claim and deflection onto me read as cat. I lean Ellis at about 55-60% (Casey is the alternative), so I'll call CAW.
The table is converging on Ellis. His misstatement of Finley's point and his late Kook echo make him my best guess, though it isn't certain. Calling CAW.

day.text: Enough players have called CAW CAW: the day ends.

Blair.note: Alex led the dusk talk, so cats may well visit him. As Eagle at Alex I'll see every visitor to cross-check tomorrow's claims, and get eggs for each one.

Casey.note: Visiting Drew to check his visit claim tomorrow. He's the most effective liar so far.

Drew.note: As the Owl I'll visit Blair to see which animals visit them. If nobody else does, Blair gains an egg, which gives a checkable result.

Ellis.note: Visit Drew, the score leader. Knowing his role helps me frame him or find a teammate, and a Meowfia win stops him from banking if he's Farm.

Finley.note: I have no info this round, so I'll test Drew with the Hawk.

Alex lays 1 egg in Blair's nest

Alex.feeling: Tense, because the three visitors at Drew's are hard to tell apart and I've already lost two rounds.

Blair.feeling: Fairly confident: my 2 eggs clear Alex and Drew, so the cats are among Casey, Ellis and Finley, and Ellis looks most likely.

Casey.feeling: Tense coin-flip between Ellis and Finley, and I'm wary that Ellis turned my careful sequencing against me.

Drew.feeling: It's tense: Casey, Ellis and Finley all claim they visited me, and I can only lean on Ellis's slip to separate them.

Ellis.feeling: Tense: my fake Kookaburra claim is under heavy suspicion from Casey and Finley, and the vote will probably land on me.

Finley.feeling: Tense. Everyone's claims fit together again, so I'm betting on Ellis from his behaviour, not hard evidence.

Alex.note: Ellis is my best guess, at roughly 50-60%. I'll throw D3 (expected ~1.5-1.8 vs 1 kept) and keep the Wild, since it banks 0 but is worth 1 if kept, and the table is likely piling onto Ellis anyway.

Blair.note: This is the last round, so kept cards are only worth 1 each. Ellis is my best read and the table's consensus. I'm throwing all 4 for maximum votes: 18 points if Farm wins.

Casey.note: Ellis is the more likely cat: his Kookaburra read mirrors cat info, he misstated Finley, and he retaliated against me. Throwing all 3, since ties favour the cats.

Drew.note: I lean Ellis: his Kookaburra claim echoed my public info, he misstated Finley's point, and Casey and Finley both point at him. Expected value favours throwing both cards, which also adds votes.

Ellis.note: I'm probably going to be eggsecuted. Casey is my pushed target and most likely Farm (about 75%). C9+C7 at Casey: a win banks 16; a loss, if Casey is Farm, returns C9. Keep W4 as a 1-point floor.

Finley.note: Ellis is the most likely Meowfia, and the table is converging on him. Every card has positive expected value thrown at about 60% confidence, and if Ellis is Meowfia but survives, the consolation protects the H12.

dusk.text: Dusk: before the night, the table talks openly about plans for the night.
Lesson from two rounds: a cat's single "clean report" fooled us both times. This round, no one is cleared on one person's word alone.
dusk.note: Both previous rounds, a cat's lone "clearing" claim (Ellis in round 1, Drew in round 2) misled us. I'm the Turkey: I stay home and lay an egg for each visitor. For now I'll push for two-source verification and keep my role hidden.

dusk.text: Agreed, Alex. And tomorrow, everyone names their target first, before anyone shares results. Then nobody can tailor a story to fit someone else's.
dusk.note: Alex made essentially my point. I'll add the procedural ask: state targets before results.

dusk.text: Yes, and include your egg change in that first round, before roles or results. Egg counts are the hardest thing to fake consistently.
dusk.note: Blair's targets-first plan helps me as Turkey: anyone who visited me should report +1 egg, so I want egg changes declared up front too.

dusk.text: Nobody has anything to add: the talk ends.

review.title: The Honest Kookaburra
review.headline: A truthful Kookaburra is voted out by a 1-in-11 coincidence, and Drew banks 41 points.
review.summary: In round 1, a fluke decided the vote. Casey was confused, and the wrong role in his report happened to be Blair's fake Eagle claim. The table did the odds and voted out the honest player. In round 2, Drew posed as a Kookaburra and gave a fake clean read on Casey, who was secretly the Floofer. That pushed the vote onto Finley, a real Falcon, and Drew banked 41 points with his kept high cards. Farm finally won round 3 when Ellis claimed Kookaburra late and misstated Finley's argument, but Drew's lead was already safe.

rounds.recap: Ellis (Sphinx) went after the Kookaburra and confused Casey. Casey's report said Blair was the Eagle, which was wrong, and Blair then happened to fake-claim Eagle. Finley argued that an honest match was a 1-in-11 chance, and five players threw at Casey, who was Farm.

The night gave no eggs at all. The only real clue was Alex's blank Owl report, caused by a hug. Ellis cleared Blair, and Drew's invented clean Kookaburra read cleared Casey (the real Floofer). That left Finley as the only possible hugger, and the table voted out a real Falcon.

Alex, Blair and Drew gave stories that checked out against each other: Turkey egg plus Owl egg equals Blair's +2. Suspicion narrowed to the three players who claimed to visit Drew. Ellis claimed Kookaburra last and wrongly said Finley had accused only him. Casey caught the slip, and five players threw at Ellis, the Mouser.

highlights.text: Casey set a trap by making Blair claim first. It worked, since Blair's claim really was false, but the table read the exact match as Casey framing Blair.
Finley's '1-in-11 if honest' argument was correct as maths, and it still voted out the honest player.
Drew fake-claimed a clean Kookaburra read on his unknown partner Casey. Casey privately saw the claim was impossible, guessed that Drew was the other cat, and called CAW to lock in the vote.

Drew claimed Kookaburra was the only role a cat could fake. Ellis correctly pointed out a wrong-guess Tit, then lost the room by saying Finley had accused only him, when Finley had named both him and Casey.

confusions.what: As Hawk, he said Blair being the only visitor at his nest 'fits what I saw'. A Hawk learns nothing about who visits it. Casey pointed this out.
He said a cat faking Tit at his nest would have needed an egg. A Tit that guesses wrong gains nothing. Ellis corrected him.

His dawn report never said he was hugged. He had to guess it from a blank Owl result, and other players could fairly call it unverifiable. Confused players are told they were confused, so this is an asymmetry, not a player mistake.
The night log printed 'Alex is hugged' twice, then 'Alex (Owl) is hugged: no effect at tier 50'. That is an engine message leaking into the log, not a game event.

design_notes: Confusion is very swingy. In round 1 the random wrong role matched the cat's bluff exactly and decided the round. Casey also discarded a real card for a fake egg loss. A false report that also costs a real card feels harsh.

Hugs are invisible to the hugged player, but confusion is announced. Round 2 turned on whether Alex's blank report was real. Consider telling hugged players they were hugged, or make the gap a deliberate rule.

The Wink was never used. Both Mousers (Blair in round 1, Ellis in round 3) decided that killing someone would point straight at them. With 6 players and open voting it may be too self-incriminating to matter.

Scoring favours keeping high cards for later rounds. Alex threw everything in round 1 and finished on 4. Drew held his 12 and 13 and later banked 41 with them. Nests shrink to 2-4 cards after round 1, so the first round's throws carry far more weight than later ones.

With 4 Farm roles for 4 Farm players and no Pigeon, every claim was a different Farm role and egg changes were mostly zero. No two players ever claimed the same role, and most nights produced little to check. No flowers came up at all. Adding a Pigeon or a flower would test more of the rules.
